<!--
Knit in RStudio or run from the repository root:
rmarkdown::render("example Rmarkdown/rmarkdown-template.rmd")

Write a new slide with ## Title, and lists with - items (indent subitems
by four spaces). Use **bold**, *italic*, math, images, and R chunks normally.
The companion template and Lua filter reuse ../cpb-beamer.sty and preserve
its layouts. Keep both companion files beside this Rmd.

Special heading attributes:
  {.split}: two columns; put the right-column divider on its own line.
  The next ## ends the slide. See split-example.rmd for PDF and HTML examples.
  {layout="title"} / {layout="end"}: CPB opening / closing slide
  {layout="section" subtitle="Subtext"}: CPB section divider
  {layout="agenda" title="Agenda"}: CPB agenda with Markdown content.
  The title argument overrides the heading; omit it to use the heading text.
  {.untitled}: hide the heading on an ordinary slide
  {.plain}: no decoration; {.noframenumbering}: do not count the slide
  {.fragile}: permit verbatim content

Use > [!BLOCK] Title to start a CPB block. Prefix each content line with >,
including blank lines. An unquoted paragraph ends the block.
The older fenced Div with class .cpb-block remains supported.
Diagram callouts use > [!DIAGRAM] magenta or blue, a three-column table,
and an optional caption paragraph. Each row becomes a box (maximum four).
The default width is 60%; append {width=80%} to change it.
Add a label with {#fig:my-diagram width=60%} for cross-references.
Raw LaTeX is needed only for exact spacing and the original
table, cross-references, and navigation buttons.
-->

## A title in the frame

- References can be used using the references.bib file.
    - You can cite \cite{lundberg2017} or \citep{lundberg2017}
- We recommend adding the Figures in the Figures folder (you can also add subfolders if needed).
    - Reference by using Figure \ref{fig:example_figure}
    - If the figures and tables order change, the numbers are automatically updated.

## Custom Rmarkdown to LaTeX diagrams

\vspace{1cm}

> [!DIAGRAM] magenta {#fig:example_diagram_magenta}
>
> | Box   | Text   | Caption   |
> |-------|--------|-----------|
> | Box 1 | Text 1 | Caption 1 |
> | Box 2 | Text 2 | Caption 2 |
> | Box 3 | Text 3 |           |
> | Box 4 | Text 4 | Caption 4 |
>
> Diagrams can be magenta or blue

<!-- separate diagrams -->

> [!DIAGRAM] blue {#fig:example_diagram_blue}
>
> | Box   | Text   | Caption   |
> |-------|--------|-----------|
> | Box 1 | Text 1 | Caption 1 |
> | Box 2 | Text 2 | Caption 2 |
> | Box 3 | Text 3 |           |
>
> Remove this line to remove the figure captions

## You can combine diagrams and text/enumerations

\vspace{1cm}

> [!DIAGRAM] magenta {#fig:example_diagram_magenta}
>
> | Box   | Text   | Caption   |
> |-------|--------|-----------|
> | Box 1 | Text 1 | Caption 1 |
> | Box 2 | Text 2 | Caption 2 |
> | Box 3 | Text 3 |           |
> | Box 4 | Text 4 | Caption 4 |


- This diagram has no Figure caption
  - It is magenta
  - But it can easily be blue
  
## Slide with table {.fragile}

\scriptsize

- You can add tables by creating a new file and adding it to the Tables folder
- You can also make reference to the objects by using Table \ref{tab:example_table}. This can be done with `Table \ref{tab:example_table}`

\pause

```{=latex}
\vspace{-0.5cm}
\begin{table}[!ht]
\begin{scriptsize}
\centering
\caption{Table example}
\scriptsize
\arrayrulecolor{cpbMagenta}
\input{Tables/RMSE_Bijstand}
\label{tab:example_table}
\end{scriptsize}
\end{table}
\vspace{0.5em}
\raggedright
\scriptsize
```

**Note:** You can also add a footnote to add information about your figure or table.

## Plain slide {#slide:label_to_frame .plain .fragile .untitled}

- You can have a slide without any decoration by using `\begin{frame}[plain]`when starting your new frame
- You can also have navigation buttons by using `\cpbbutton{appendix:01}{Go to Appendix}{inline}` \cpbbutton{appendix:01}{Go to Appendix}{inline}
- The position options are `inline, bottom left, bottom right`

- You can use these Appendix slides to add extra information
- Navigation can be done with buttons that link to other slides
